commits.message:
Merge N3b R2: repair acceptance receipts that record a rejected member

The receipt-rejections migration becomes 0016, after the confirmed-ledger merges (0014) and the derived settlement status (0015).
Merge N3f: hold native restore refusals by cause in every history recovery caller
Merge N6b: settlement status derived from the intent journal, orphaned activity records pruned
Merge N5: temporal confirmed ledger, merges finalized by delta

Hold native restore refusals by cause in every history recovery caller

The signed-header recovery let a native restore refusal fail the history owner with no readiness reason, and every restore failure was relabelled as an unretained root, so a capped index or a transient store read looked like missing state.

The signed-header recovery now holds a native restore refusal under its own readiness source instead of failing the history owner, and skips the landed-block rebase in the pass it holds. A failed restore is named by its real cause: a target closure that is not in the store, a full index over FULL_INDEX_MAX_RECORDS or FULL_INDEX_MAX_BYTES (naming the cap and its value), or a transient store read that a later restore retries. The correction rewind, release, revival and signed-header callers hold each under a named reason and clear it on the next success.

Repair acceptance receipts that record a rejected member

Before the commit-stage closure, a commit-stage or speculative rejection removed a transaction and wrote its rejection row without reversing the acceptance receipt that held it. A later closure over that receipt then failed on the gone member, and the landed-block rebase stayed failed until an operator intervened.

Migration 0014 records each member of an unreversed acceptance receipt that has a terminal rejection row. The batch closure reads a recorded member that is no longer pending as decided. The working-ledger rebuild rejects the pending members of each recorded receipt with no undecided member as batch members, and recordRejections reverses every recorded receipt whose members are all decided and drops its recorded rows. A repair whose batch rejections reach an undecided member is not applied.

A closure that meets a member that is neither pending, settled, nor recorded rejected fails with UndecidedBatchMember; the rebase raises it as the readiness reason landed_block_batch_undecided, and the rebase failure record carries its reason and detail.

Derive settlement status from the intent journal and prune orphaned activity records (#804)

A settlement attempt is no longer stored confirmed at the
confirmation depth. It stays pending and its level is read from the
intent journal every tick, so a rollback below the confirmation depth
puts the job's phase back. Only the follower prune step writes final,
once the attempt's transaction is deeper than k, and the retention
hold lasts until then. A new attempt is refused while any attempt
reads open, under the owner-row lock. The restored-fee and generation
recheck machinery is deleted.

Orphaned operator activity records are cleared in the follower prune
step's transaction, with a prune floor holding them through a replay.

Make confirmed_ledger temporal and finalize merges by delta (#803)

A landed merge now folds into confirmed_ledger as a stored delta keyed
by the merge: spent rows move to node_confirmed_ledger_spent, produced
rows are inserted and the event marks are recorded, so a rollback
unfolds it exactly. Stored deltas are released only once the merge is
below the follower's pruned-through slot, where no rollback can reach
it. Merge finalization no longer rewrites or locks the whole ledger.

A fold onto the wrong base is held as confirmed_ledger_base_mismatch
and writes nothing; the frontier is bound by header identity, never
re-anchored on an equal root. Both merge finalization paths and the
startup repair refuse a journal that is not bound to its canonical
header. Landed-block processing reads the ledger only when it
processes a new row.
Merge N3b R1: apply the rejection closure to commit-stage rejections and carry inclusion marks through skipped submissions
Merge N3e: compare the displacement aggregate's root and hold an unretained target root

Apply the working-ledger rejection closure to commit-stage rejections

A commit-stage rejection now runs closeRejections in one transaction:
pending spenders of a rejected output are rejected as dependents,
pending co-members of an unreversed acceptance receipt holding a
rejected transaction are rejected as batch members, and the receipts
are reversed by recordRejections. Rows marked by a block are settled.
A closure that reaches a transaction Phase B accepted for the block
being built removes it from the candidates and runs Phase B again.
The separate dependent cascade is removed.

The skipped-submission transfer moves mempool rows to the processed
mempool in one statement that carries included_by.

Compare the base journal's expected root before taking its aggregate, and hold a native restore refused as not retained on the release and revival paths

Displacement compensation with no returned prefix now takes the base journal's UTxO payload aggregate only when that journal's expected root is the target root, through the helper the displaced-chain repair already uses. A NativeMpfRootNotRetained refusal on the signed-intent release, the displaced-chain rewind, the displacement compensation or the retained displacement's inverse is held under the caller's source as signed_intent_target_root_not_retained, with the plan prepared and retried on every evaluation. The cause-chain matcher moves to history-dependent-recovery so the correction rewind and these holds share it.

Give the node's follower test database cleanup an explicit hook budget

dropAll drops each database a suite created one at a time with FORCE, and a fork-sim that creates a store per run outgrew the 10 s hook default on a loaded CI runner (l1-operator-set-fork-sim's afterAll timed out on 4d7da9845). Every suite on the shared helper now gives its cleanup the same budget the committee suites use.
Merge I1d: hold the intent prune floor through a replay and journal in-node list inserts

Hold the intent journal's prune floor through a replay and journal in-node list inserts

While the tracked-set record says replaying, the intent journal declares a class A prune floor at its prune mark's boundary (or, with no mark, where the replay began); the first prune step after the replay ends sets none.

The genesis deposit and the atomic protocol initialization are journaled as the list_insert family, keyed by event key and one-shot nonce. Their predicate is wanted while the follower's facts show the insert's target unreached: the event key absent from the never-reuse key set, no live state-queue policy output. Submissions from CLI-only paths go out unjournaled with reason no_follower, the only unjournaled reason left.
